validity.researcher_notes: This row is a PROJECT, not the REX system: the 'Critical Energy Reliability Link' (CERL), a proposed REX expansion (FERC Docket CP25-539-000, applicants Rockies Express Pipeline LLC / Cheyenne Connector, LLC / East Cheyenne Gas Storage, LLC) to serve Colorado Springs Utilities, filed 2025-08-15. Existence confirmed independently: the Federal Register notice of application (federalregister.gov, 90 FR 42758, 2025-09-04) states the same scope, and the operator's own project site (criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com) and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (Aug 2026 release, row 31, docket CP25-539-000) both corroborate it as an active, real application. No duplicate: none of the other 41 rows in this batch's roster is REX or CERL, and REX's other rows (mainline, Entrega phases, REX-East) are swept in slice 1 / other batches, not this roster -- no double-count risk found. Classification correct: NGA section 7(b)/7(c) interstate certificate application = transmission-jurisdictional (PipelineType=transmission), commodity natural gas (Fuel=Gas). Caveats, each filed as its own record below: StartYear1 is wrong (sheet 2027, sourced true in-service year is 2028 -- see the spec concern below); ConstructionYear, SegmentCost, Diameter and Owner1/2/3-only-Operator support in this shard rest on a single verified origin each (the FERC docket / operator's own site), so they are staged at medium tier pending a second independent source. Of the 30 wiki-harvested citations for this gem.wiki page, only 2 (oilandgaswatch.org and criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com) concern THIS 2025 project; the other 28 are about the historical 2005-2020 REX mainline (original construction, Entrega phases I/II, Kinder Morgan/Sempra/ConocoPhillips/Tallgrass ownership transactions) and do not apply to this segment -- checked their titles/dates/context against the CERL scope and none names or states a value for the Critical Energy Reliability Link Project. Orchestrator note: proposed_refs were empty on this record while it claimed tier=high / independent=true. A validity record carries no verifications by convention, so its tier is counted over proposed_refs -- an empty list reads as zero publishers and contradicts the claimed tier. The three sources the prose already names as independently confirming existence (federalregister.gov 90 FR 42758; criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com, the operator's own project site; eia.gov Aug-2026 release, row 31) are now listed, which is what the high/independent claim actually rests on: three distinct publishers.

The project's own site (criticalenergyreliabilitylink.com) states verbatim: 'The project is expected to commence construction in the second quarter of 2027 and be placed in-service in the second quarter of 2028.' EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (every release Oct 2025 through Aug 2026, 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet, row 31/30) carries 'Year In Service Date' = 2028 for this exact project (docket CP25-539-000). Both agree on 2028 as the in-service year and neither supports 2027 as an in-service date -- 2027 is the construction-START year per the operator's own description. This is a material disagreement (not a rounding difference), so staged as a spec concern rather than silently corrected. The existing [ref] (oilandgaswatch.org) does not state either year -- it is a JS-rendered page whose HTML shell (fetched via curl and WebFetch) carries no readable pipeline-specific text, so it never actually supported this cell; the Start [ref] fill below carries the corrected value with new sources.
